SOCIAL MEDIA AND EXTERNAL COMMUNICATIONS POLICY

Quillon Therapeutics, Inc.
Adopted by the Board of Directors on July 8, 2026
Owner: General Counsel and Chief Communications Officer
Applies to: all directors, officers, employees, and contractors

1. PURPOSE

This policy states who may speak for Quillon Therapeutics, Inc. and how everyone else may talk about the company in public, including on social media. It protects the company's confidential information, keeps its public statements accurate and consistent with its securities-law obligations, and — just as importantly — protects each person's right to talk about their own pay and working conditions.

2. YOUR PROTECTED RIGHTS

Nothing in this policy limits any right you have under Section 7 of the National Labor Relations Act to discuss your wages, hours, benefits, or other terms and conditions of employment with coworkers or with anyone else, on social media or anywhere else. Nothing in this policy prevents you from reporting a possible violation of law to the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, the Department of Justice, or any other government agency, from participating in an agency investigation, or from receiving a whistleblower award. You do not need the company's permission to do any of this, and you do not need to tell the company you have done it. This section controls over anything else in this policy that could be read to conflict with it.

3. WHO MAY SPEAK FOR THE COMPANY

Only the Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Financial Officer, the Chief Communications Officer, and the Investor Relations lead are authorized to speak for the company to investors, analysts, or the news media. No one else may make a statement on the company's behalf, respond to a media inquiry, or post from a company-branded account without the Chief Communications Officer's approval. Forward a media inquiry to press@quillontx.example the same day you receive it.

4. REGULATION FD AND MATERIAL NONPUBLIC INFORMATION

Regulation FD prohibits selective disclosure of material nonpublic information about the company. Do not post, comment on, or share anything about the company's clinical results, regulatory interactions, financing, partnerships, or financial performance before the company has disclosed it publicly. Do not confirm, deny, or hint at a rumor. If the company designates a social media channel for Regulation FD disclosure, it will say so in a Form 8-K first, as the SEC's 2013 guidance requires.

5. QUIET PERIODS

During any quiet period the General Counsel announces — before an earnings release, during a securities offering, or around a material transaction — do not post anything about the company's performance, prospects, or the transaction.

6. CLINICAL AND SCIENTIFIC CLAIMS

Do not make a claim about the safety or efficacy of any company product candidate. Product candidates are investigational and are not approved by the Food and Drug Administration, and a statement suggesting otherwise can be an unlawful pre-approval promotion under 21 C.F.R. § 312.7. Refer any scientific question to Medical Affairs.

7. YOUR PERSONAL ACCOUNTS

You are free to have personal accounts and to say you work at Quillon. If you post about the company or the industry, make clear you are speaking for yourself — a simple "views my own" in your profile is enough. Do not use the company logo or a company-branded image on a personal account. Do not speak in a way that would lead a reasonable reader to think the company is speaking.

8. ENDORSEMENTS AND DISCLOSURE

If you post about the company's products or about a company with which we have a business relationship, disclose your connection clearly and conspicuously in the post itself, as the FTC's Endorsement Guides, 16 C.F.R. Part 255, require. "#employee" or "I work at Quillon" in the body of the post is sufficient; a disclosure buried in a thread or behind a "more" link is not. The same applies to anyone we pay or give free product to; the Chief Communications Officer maintains the disclosure language for influencer engagements.

9. CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION AND OTHERS' PRIVACY

Do not post confidential company information, and do not post information a partner, investigator, or vendor gave us in confidence. Do not post anything about an identifiable patient or study subject. Do not post a photograph taken inside a laboratory or manufacturing area without approval.

10. RESPECT

Harassing, threatening, or discriminatory posts directed at a coworker violate the company's anti-harassment policy wherever they are made. Disagreement about the company or its management is not harassment, and this section is not to be applied to discourage the discussion Section 2 protects.

11. IF YOU MAKE A MISTAKE

Tell the Chief Communications Officer. Do not delete a post about the company without asking first — a deletion can itself become an issue, and the company may have a duty to preserve it. Nobody is disciplined for reporting a mistake promptly and in good faith.

12. MONITORING

The company monitors public channels for mentions of its name and products. It does not require access to your personal accounts, does not ask for your passwords, and does not ask you to add anyone from the company to a personal account, as Tennessee Code Annotated section 50-1-1003 and comparable laws in other states provide.

13. CONSEQUENCES

A violation of this policy, other than conduct Section 2 protects, may result in discipline up to and including termination.

14. QUESTIONS

Ask the Chief Communications Officer or the General Counsel.
